title: Generative Conjectures: Learning Science and Teaching Our Children Well
author: Terry U
summary: A rigorous scholarly essay arguing that the Science of Reading movement has committed a category error: using cognitive/neural evidence (lab-level claims) to warrant classroom-level prescriptions (pedagogical claims). Through a synthesis of three foundational learning science papers — Collins (1990), Edelson (2002), and Sandoval (2014) — the author shows that design-based research is the correct methodology for answering pedagogical questions. Scripted phonics programs cannot tell you which of two types of failure has occurred; conjecture mapping can.
points: Core error: cognitive science can tell us children need phonics; it cannot tell us how to teach phonics in real classrooms with real children in real communities.

Collins (1990): design experiments require working with teachers as co-investigators, no vested interest in outcomes, and recognition that 'relations of community to school' only become visible at larger grain sizes.
Edelson (2002): domain theories (descriptive — how the world works) are distinct from design frameworks (prescriptive — how to build learning environments); they require different kinds of evidence.

Sandoval (2014): conjecture mapping gives learning science its argumentative grammar — design conjectures (does the embodiment produce the mediating process?) vs. theoretical conjectures (does the mediating process produce the outcome?).

A scripted phonics program that fails could be failing in two distinct ways: wrong activity design (design conjecture failure) or wrong theory of how decoding becomes reading (theoretical conjecture failure). Scripts can't distinguish these; conjecture maps can.

The Science of Reading captured state legislation by offering a pipeline that could be legislated; learning science offers university-school partnerships and iterative design — less photogenic but more warranted.

Existing examples: Strategic Education Research Partnership (SERP), National Network of Education Research-Practice Partnerships (NNERPP, 79 active partnerships), National Center for Research in Policy and Practice (NCRPP).
quotes: The Science of Reading makes classroom prescriptions that only design-based research is equipped to warrant. The root issue is not experimentalism; the issue is the alignment of claims to warrants.
Sandoval gives learning science its own grammar, one suited to the kinds of claims it actually makes about classrooms, teachers, children, and the conditions under which learning happens.

The conflation that opened this essay is, finally, a confusion about what the question even is. Whether children need phonics is settled. How to teach phonics in real classrooms, to real children, in ways that produce real readers and sustain real love of language, is an unsettled question.
